behavior: `mergeProps` and `mergePropsN` treat the result of a props function as a set. Each handler that the function returns gets the Vase UI event. `event.preventVaseUIHandler()` then does not throw when no later set has a handler for that event. An array of handlers that the function returns becomes one handler. The merge copies the result, so a later set does not change an object that the function returns. Such an object can be a constant or a reactive object. A function in the first set gets a new object, and `mergePropsN([])` returns a new object. A write to one of them does not reach another call. In Base UI, the type of such a handler has `preventBaseUIHandler()`. The event has no such method when no later set has a handler for that event. A later set writes to the object that a function in a later argument returns. Each function in the first set and each `mergePropsN([])` call get the same object.
